summary: A retained room candidate's polygons are already metres in the plan-local frame: the vector reader applied (pdf - originPdf) * metresPerPdfPoint with y flipped before retention. planFrame records how the metres were made; it is not a transform still to apply. The written rule (polygon area x scale squared) gives a 0.0076 m2 kitchen; the polygon's own area gives 6.55 m2 against the plan's stated 8' x 8'11" (6.63 m2). Nothing was built.

builder.how: Room candidates are not shaped at read time: projectBuilding copies record.body.canonicalCandidates verbatim into building.candidates, then finishBuilding hashes the projection (projectionDigest, line 163) and parses NormalizedBuildingSchema. The candidate itself is shaped by the caller of retain_rooms (docs/evidence/gf-backend/k2c/rooms-through-api.ts:37-51) and stored by commandTx.
builder.revisionNote: planEstimate added in projectBuilding enters projectionDigest, so Magnolia's canonical revisionId changes once at deploy; clients holding the old expectedCanonicalRevision get the existing 'Refresh the current canonical building' conflict.

schemaReaders.use: retain_rooms request extends the schema (strict); needs planEstimate: z.never().optional() so a caller cannot supply it
NormalizedBuildingSchema.candidates (the canonical read); optional field is additive
parses stored canonicalCandidates; stored rows never carry planEstimate because it would be added only at read

units.polygons: metres, plan-local panel frame: x = page_right from planFrame.originPdf, y = page_up (PDF y flipped), unplaced
units.producer: services/geo/geo/vector_plan.py:1248-1279 _metric_payload: affinity.translate(-origin) then scale(xfact=s, yfact=-s); polygonMetres is what the k2c caller retained as polygons
units.planFrameApplies: planFrame.originPdf and metresPerPdfPoint map PDF points (the citation's region) into the polygon's frame; they do not apply to the polygon's coordinates, which are already the result.
units.proof: For all 18 rooms the polygon's bbox equals the citation region (pt, top-left y-down) mapped through ((x - ox) * s, (oy - y) * s) to within 1e-6 m.
units.realData: every room is one polygon with one ring; no holes or multipart rooms on Magnolia

plausibility.byWrittenRule: implausible: areas 0.002-0.027 m2, extents 0.04-0.22 m for kitchens, bedrooms and a terrace
plausibility.asStored: plausible: of 10 rooms with a parsed stated product, 9 are within 0.13 m2 (1.1%) of it (room inside walls vs drawn face); MASTER BEDROOM (first floor) is 15.94 m2 against a stated 12'6" x 15'10" = 18.39 m2, the same literal as the ground floor's DINING AND LIVING, so the label pairing or the drawing differs and stays a finding, not a correction

missing: A lead decision on the rule. Proposed: areaM2 = the polygon's own area (outer rings minus holes, summed), extentM = its bbox width and height, both already metres; basis keeps method, scaleState and metresPerPdfPoint as the provenance of how the drawing was scaled, with the method renamed (for example 'polygon_area_in_plan_metres@1') because nothing is multiplied by the scale at read time. The estimate stays 'unknown' when planFrame is absent, since then the polygon's unit is not established.
